description:
Maintainer sequencing instruction, 2026-08-11: 'once the marviken tests land for the HEM model, then implement the drift flux and 6 equation version in tampines'. HOLD — do not start until the tampines-steam-tables fleet lands the Marviken HEM gate and the coordinator releases this work.

Why the order matters: the HEM result is the reference the higher-fidelity versions are compared against. Same nozzle geometry, same initial conditions, same Marviken test numbers, same reference data — only the model changes; building in parallel from a different reading of NUREG/CR-2671 would make the cross-fidelity comparison meaningless.

When released: take the case setup from the tampines-steam-tables Marviken implementation VERBATIM rather than re-deriving from the report. Source is catalogued in kovan as nrc1982marviken (open tier, US NRC publication). Test-ownership split: tampines-steam-tables owns HEM tests; tampines owns drift-flux and 6-equation tests.

Note the six-equation model itself does not exist in tampines yet (two_fluid.rs is a deliberate NotYetImplemented scaffold, op-dt3.13/op-dt3.19), so the 6-eqn Marviken test is doubly blocked.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
UNBLOCKED 2026-08-11 — the sibling HEM Marviken reference has landed (bead op-21g.16, crates/tampines-steam-tables/src/steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/tests/marviken_tests.rs, 6 active tests, ~1.4 s).

READ THE MODULE //! DOC OF THAT FILE FIRST. It states the full reproducible case setup (nozzle 500 mm bore / 166 mm long / L/D = 0.3, converging only, rounded 250 mm-radius inlet; steam dome 4.96 MPa / Tsat 263 degC; vessel water 260 degC for test 23 and 230 degC for test 24 = 3 K and 33 K nominal subcooling, NUREG/CR-2671 Table 4:2 rows 3-6; discharge into containment, peak 236/328 kPa, back pressure assumed 1 atm and shown immaterial since the lowest choke pressure is 2.774 MPa), the data provenance and digitisation uncertainty, the error budget, and a numbered lessons section written specifically for this bead.

HEM reference numbers to compare against (measured 2026-08-11, v0.2.5, release):
- crate HEM dispatcher: test 23 mean |dev| 12.6 % / signed +5.9 % / max 23.1 % (VALIDATED); test 24 mean |dev| 48.6 % / signed -48.5 % / max 70.2 % (NOT validated).
- bare HEM maximum-mass-flux criterion: test 23 mean 10.1 % / signed -10.1 %; test 24 mean 9.0 % / signed -1.8 %.
Use the BARE-CRITERION numbers as the HEM reference for the three-fidelity comparison. The dispatcher's test-24 deficit is a branch-selection defect (bead op-dqng), not HEM physics, and comparing against it would flatter drift-flux for the wrong reason.

Falsifiable expectation recorded there: a non-equilibrium model should NOT gain much on the subcooled branch (HEM is already unbiased there once the right branch is taken). It should gain at the flashing-inception knee of test 24 (3.0-3.3 MPa, where HEM over-predicts up to +26.5 % then under-predicts up to -18.2 %, i.e. puts the knee at too high a pressure) and on test 23's saturated branch (uniform -10.1 % bias, the L/D < 1.5 length effect NUREG/CR-2671 section 9.2 reports).

Tolerance: +/-25 % per point, +/-15 % on the mean. The dominant error term is experimental scatter (+/-12.9 % for test 23, +/-20.0 % for test 24, measured), not digitisation (RMS 6.3 %) and not numerics (<0.001 %). Do not read a 10 % result as better than a 15 % one on this dataset.

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content:
Marviken drift-flux gates WRITTEN AND MEASURED, 2026-08-11 (~17:00 SGT). All work in crates/tampines/src/multiphase_1d/marviken_tests.rs; case setup taken verbatim from the sibling HEM reference per the maintainer instruction; compared against the BARE HEM maximum-mass-flux criterion baseline as instructed (dispatcher excluded, op-dqng).

EXPLORATION FIRST (marviken_drift_flux_explore, run before any assertion was written, at 5 stagnation points 2.829/3.150/3.725/4.772/4.975 MPa): NO interior maximum anywhere — the steady flux rises monotonically down to the 101.325 kPa containment pressure, as anticipated for a semi-implicit pressure-based scheme with no imposed choking criterion (the RELAP5 situation). 68/69 sweeps in the full gates have no interior maximum; the single exception (4.306 MPa, t24) wins by 0.3 % = plateau noise. What IS measurable is an effective plateau: over the lower half of the sweep (factor ~20 in receiver pressure) the flux moves by mean 4.9 % / worst 5.2 % (t23) and 3.2 % / 7.3 % (t24). Documented as a limitation of the method, not papered over. Sweep cost 2.9-12.4 s per point; no trimming of sweep, t_end or dt was needed or done.

GATE RESULTS (MarvikenCase::default: 8 cells, dt 20 us, t_end 12 ms, C0 1.13, Vgj 0.1, tau 1 ms; 897 marched transients, 0 refused steps, max Courant 0.326):
- Test 23 (3 K): mean |dev| 8.9 %, signed +2.8 %, max 19.7 %, 0/29 points outside +/-25 % -> VALIDATED (both criteria met). vs bare HEM 10.1 % / -10.1 % / 28.2 %: drift flux clearly wins; HEM's uniform -10.1 % saturated-branch bias becomes +2.8 % (the L/D<1.5 length-effect regime of NUREG/CR-2671 sec 9.2).
- Test 24 (33 K): mean |dev| 11.4 %, signed -9.7 %, max 28.8 %, 6/40 points outside +/-25 % -> NOT VALIDATED, kept as an honest CHARACTERISATION test (mean criterion met, per-point criterion missed; all 6 misses clustered in 3.121-3.418 MPa and the gate asserts that clustering). vs bare HEM 9.0 % / -1.8 % / 26.5 %: drift flux slightly loses.

FALSIFIABLE EXPECTATION (recorded here 04:26): (1) no gain on the deeply subcooled branch — SUPPORTED (11 points >= 4.00 MPa: mean 4.3 %, signed -2.3 % vs HEM -1.8 %); (2) gain at the t24 flashing-inception knee with the knee moving down and sharpening — REFUTED: the model removes HEM's over-prediction below 3.10 MPa (signed +0.1 % over 9 points vs HEM up to +26.5 %) but FLATTENS the knee, systematic -23.0 % across 3.10-3.46 MPa, worse than HEM's -18.2 % (measured envelope +143 % over 2.984-3.418 MPa, model +65 %); (3) gain on t23's saturated branch — SUPPORTED, and it is where the whole t23 win comes from.

Knee deficit deliberately NOT attributed: single-tau relaxation, the constant-area domain (no convergent inlet resolved) and the absent interfacial-area/wall-nucleation model are all live candidates this test set cannot separate. No coefficient (C0, Vgj, tau, DEEP_SUBCOOLING_RATIO), tolerance, reference constant or data array was changed; a tau study is explicitly deferred as fitting to the validation set.

WALL CLOCK: 98.1 s (t23) / 381 s (t24), separate #[test] fns so cargo parallelises them. Cleanup done: unused AvailableEnergy import removed, print_sweep wired into both gates, cargo check -p tampines --lib --tests --release clean with zero warnings.

VERIFICATION BY ORCHESTRATOR: independent full run 'cargo test --release -p tampines --lib multiphase_1d' -> 9 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, finished in 590.66s (agents' runs: 380-416 s; slower here under concurrent compile load from an unrelated session). Module //! doc and both gate doc comments carry methodology AND measured results per the workspace V&V rule. Left open here: nothing on the drift-flux side; the six-equation Marviken test remains blocked on op-62vf/op-dt3.13 and two_fluid_tests.rs stays the 12-line placeholder. Not closing this bead — maintainer decision.

description:
Literally zero code in the workspace, and it is the single most important closure for HTR-10 passive safety behaviour — it sets how fast decay heat conducts radially out of the bed when forced cooling is lost.

SCOPE: an effective conductivity model summing the solid, stagnant-gas, particle-contact and radiation contributions, with the near-wall region correction where bed voidage rises and the correlation changes. Radiation matters increasingly at the high temperatures reached in a loss-of-forced-cooling transient, so it cannot be dropped.

Depends on graphite properties. Validate against published packed-bed afterheat-removal experiment data — German AVR-era and THTR-era packed-bed heat-transfer experiments are the relevant open source. Record the measured comparison with uncertainty in the test doc comment.
title: HTR-10: pebble-bed effective radial thermal conductivity

PRE-BUILD AUDIT (workspace hard rule -- search before building), what already exists so nothing here is re-invented:

  - The TRANSIENT column physics already exists and is validated: crates/outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs/src/columns/dynamic.rs (866 lines), bead op-6rhz, status Done. DynamicColumn::from_solver_input + step_rk4 + integrate_to_steady; its own test (dynamic_column_relaxes_to_steady_mesh_solution) relaxes an 8-stage benzene/toluene column to the independently-computed steady MESH solution to 4e-4 K / 9.3e-6 mole fraction / 1e-3 mol/s product split. This is NOT a DWSIM port by design (DWSIM RigorousColumn is steady-only) -- it is the textbook dynamic-distillation formulation (Luyben 2013 ch.3 / Skogestad 1997), reusing only ColumnThermo for VLE/enthalpy.
  - The STEADY MESH cascade underneath it (columns/{model,solver,bubble_point,newton_raphson,sum_rates,tridiagonal,initial_estimates}.rs, 11,355 lines) already IS the DWSIM RigorousColumn.vb port. So 'translate anything from dwsim source you need' has nothing left to translate for this task -- the port is already there and this GUI consumes it.

  - ONE real gap: the benzene()/toluene() Component data the validated dynamic-column test uses is pub(crate) inside columns::thermo_bridge::tests, not a public constructor an example crate can call.
  - NOT the same task as bead op-3sk7 ('transient crude distillation unit (CDU) example on the dynamic column') -- op-3sk7 is petroleum-assay pseudo-components with side draws, dwsim-libs-internal example/integration-test scope, unrelated GUI. description:
Found while doing op-dt3.26 (extending interfaces::checked). These panics are NOT envelope violations, so no bounds-checking facade can exclude them - the honest fix is in the solvers themselves.

PANIC SITES (traced 2026-08-11):
  - steam_turbine_equations/converging_diverging_nozzles/choked_flow/mod.rs:241
    panic!('unable to find bracket for critical mass flux root finding') - fires when
    the downward pressure scan from p0 finds no sign change in
    (g_energy - g_hem). Reached from get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_multiphase_ph
    and thus from TampinesSteamTableCV::get_crit_pressure_and_massflux.
  - converging_diverging_nozzles/joule_thomson.rs:157 panic!('bounds are same sign!')
  - converging_diverging_nozzles/joule_thomson.rs:201 panic!('Joule-Thomson algorithm:
    failed to converge')

WHY A FACADE CANNOT HELP. Whether a bracket exists is a property of the function over
the whole scan interval, not of the stagnation state (p0, h0). Deciding it requires
running the scan - at which point you have done the work and can just return the
failure. A checked wrapper that gated only the (p,h) envelope of the stagnation state
would claim a safety it does not provide, which op-dt3.26's no-half-gating rule
forbids. So interfaces::checked deliberately leaves these alone and says so in its
'Known gaps' section.

WHAT op-dt3.26 DID COVER in this area: ps::try_mass_flux_ps_eqm_throat, which is a
genuine envelope check - the unchecked mass_flux_ps_eqm_throat differentiates v(p,s)
by finite difference (dp = p*1e-5), so it evaluates the (p,s) flash at p, p+dp and
max(p-dp, floor). Near 100 MPa and near the 1073.15 K isotherm the step walks out of
the envelope and the raw function panics; the checked version re-runs the envelope
check at all three pressures (and gates the s_tp_eqm_two_phase bubble-point lookup)
and rejects instead. Verified: 162 394 accepted points, zero leaked panics.

PROPOSED FIX (needs maintainer sign-off - it CHANGES PUBLIC SIGNATURES and so was out
of scope for op-dt3.26's additive-only remit):
  - a NonConvergent-style error variant (the crate CLAUDE.md already forbids papering
    over NonConvergent with a default value, so an error type is the intended shape)
  - get_critical_pressure_and_mass_flux_* -> Result
  - the Joule-Thomson root finder -> Result
  - TampinesSteamTableCV::get_crit_pressure_and_massflux gets a try_ sibling
Alternatively keep the panicking functions and add try_ siblings that return Result,
which would stay additive.
title: tampines-steam-tables: choked-flow and Joule-Thomson solvers should return Result, not panic on non-convergence
